_: Written by `ci-video narrate`. Records which line each mp3 is a read of, so a later edit to scene.narration can be detected instead of silently keeping the old recording. Commit this with the mp3s.

map-quality.text: Three tiers of map quality, and the app names what the next one needs: keyframes, streamed while you scan.

open.text: The scan leaves your phone. It lands on your own server.

choose-your-path.text: Scan a room with the camera, or upload a walkthrough video you already have.

ftue-permissions.text: The camera sees the room, motion tracks you, and a slow sweep keeps tracking locked.

ftue-capture-modes.text: Tap a frame, auto-capture as you walk, or stream keyframes.

ftue-quality.text: You know when a room is finished scanning, before you walk out of it.

ftue-finish.text: When you're done, export the scan and open it in the desktop editor.

live-scan.text: Walk the room and the map fills in, with coverage scored live as you go.

objects-named.text: Objects come back named and placed, identified on hardware you own.

review-and-export.text: Review everything the scan found, then export it as a file you own.

world-editor.text: Every room you scan lands in one 3D world, stored on your own server.

semantic-world.text: The map is not just geometry. Every object keeps the label it was given.

what-you-get.text: It runs in the browser on your phone and sends scans to your own server.

close.text: Companion Scan, from Companion Intelligence. UnCloud your life.

pain-measure.text: How wide is that alcove? You have lived here four years, and the honest answer is that you would have to go and measure it.

pain-not-a-file.text: Your photos are files. Your messages are files. The place all of it happened in is the one thing you have never captured.

quit.text: The tools that fix this want a lidar rig, a subscription, and a copy of your floor plan on somebody else's server. Most people quit right about here.

title.text: There is a shorter way, and it needs the phone already in your pocket.

two-ways-in.text: Walk a room with the camera, or hand it a walkthrough video you already have.

the-walk.text: It asks you for one thing. Sweep the room slowly, and the map fills in behind you.

what-it-watches.text: It watches the light, the reflections and the gaps, and it tells you before you walk out of the room.

the-meter.text: Coverage is scored while you walk, off the point count itself. It goes from sparse to good, and the app is the thing that says so.

one-world.text: Every room you scan lands in one world, on a machine in your house. Three rooms here. Sixty-nine thousand points, and fifteen objects that came back named.

named-not-numbered.text: The map is not just geometry. Every object keeps the label it was given, and the confidence it was given with.

pick-a-room.text: Pick any room and the camera flies to it. Its name, its confidence and its tags are all yours to change.

how-good-a-map.text: Three tiers of map quality, and the app names exactly what the next one would need.

what-stays-yours.text: It runs in the browser on your phone, and it sends the scan to hardware you can point at.
